ex: In the novel, a cabal of palace advisers secretly plots to seize the throne.
Critics claimed a cabal of insiders was secretly running the club.

why: Example used the 'cabal of bankers controlling the world' trope, a well-known antisemitic conspiracy theme

set.def: to involve yourself or someone else completely in an activity or subject

why: Def was intransitive ('to become') but the verb is transitive (immerse yourself/someone in)
'periodically' means at regular intervals, the opposite of sporadic

cloze.s: Having grown up poor, she was ___ aware of how hard it is to pay the rent.

why: Cloze 'watching ___' used a different sense (closely/eagerly) from the def, and 'discreetly' could also fill it

ex: The injured hiker lay inert on the trail until the medics arrived.
The committee has been inert for months, and nothing on its list has been done.

why: Example illogical: patient already on the stretcher before the medics arrived

ex: There was no discernible difference between the two paint colors.
Without her glasses, Yuki saw only a faint shape in the fog, barely discernible against the gray.

why: Example 'barely make out a discernible shape' was redundant and awkward

ex: The coach's speech included an allusion to the story of David and Goliath before the big game.
Her line about a “house divided” was an allusion to a famous speech by Abraham Lincoln.

why: Calling a boss 'the emperor' is a nickname/metaphor, not an allusion to an outside work or event

ex: The museum's macabre display of skulls and old execution tools made some visitors feel sick.
Hannah has a macabre sense of humor and loves jokes about funerals.

why: Surgical tools are not about death; example did not show the meaning
